items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: That’s why I play these guys all kinds of stuff. They love it. And Gadd and those guys.

ctx.x: Yeah. They send you a track and you can add. Yeah. I have another quote here. I’m sure the studio scene, as you mentioned, has changed a lot. And this is from your James Taylor bandmate, Lou Marini. And he was talking about the way songs are put together these days, and he said, “When I listen to these vocoder vocals and the rhythm tracks you could just as easily be listening to a washing machine. Luis Conte is a master percussionist. He’s always playing stuff for us from African tribal music, Caribbean,…

Totally agreed. Of course. Man, you know what I call – and I work on some of these, I could tell you some things that man, what are some of these, you know the modern music that you hear on the radio. It sounds like wallpaper music to me. That’s what I call it. I call it wallpaper music. It’s just wallpaper. It’s almost – you know do you notice the wallpaper? No? So, it doesn’t matter. There’s like a formula. And it’s not only sad man, you have this one artist becomes a huge hit, now you have every record company…
first chorus, I play, let’s say I play congas, I play whatever, three, four, five instruments. “Okay we got it.”
